prompt:
Use case: product-mockup / compositing.
Reference 1 supplies the Utkal maritime graphical storytelling. Reference 2 supplies natural golden Tasar silk texture only.
Create ONE new TRADITIONAL LONG JHULA / JHOLA shoulder-sling bag concept, clearly different in construction from the two-handle tote references. It has ONE broad continuous LONG fabric shoulder strap joining the two upper side seams, suitable for carrying low at the hip or cross-body. No paired tote handles, no short handles, no rigid shopping-bag silhouette. A taller soft portrait pouch body, about 32 cm wide by 43 cm high in proposed proportions, with a soft folded bottom and relaxed cloth drape. Single long shoulder strap about 105-115 cm total, width roughly 5 cm, all visible.
Natural undyed golden-beige Tasar silk outer: fine irregular slub weave, subtle muted silk lustre, soft hand, NOT jute or burlap, no shiny satin. Plain cotton lining glimpsed inside the loose top opening; reinforced strap attachments; discreet cloth loop and small simple button closure. Narrow laterite fabric piping along the sides and strap edges, restrained and elegant, not a heavy patterned border.
Put the cup's SAILING STORY on the bag front: large clearly readable deep Nila Sagara uppercase serif "UTKAL" above a graceful traditional sailing boat with laterite sails, sea-blue linework waves and birds, straw sun, a few distant palms/shore details. Faithfully echo the source composition, adapted to the tall pouch. Artwork concentrated in the central/lower front, leaving generous untouched silk around it. No huge solid-colour panel, no book emblem in place of the story, no explanatory paragraph, no extra text or certification marks.
Photoreal premium product study: bag hanging naturally by its single long strap on a simple wooden wall peg, the FULL strap from peg to side attachments and full bag in frame, warm ivory lime-plaster wall, soft daylight and gentle shadows. The hanging bag should drape and crease naturally rather than stand stiffly. Portrait-oriented editorial photograph, no person, no cups, no other bags, no measurement labels, no watermark. This is a contemporary traditional-form concept, not an assertion of a specific historical craft construction.
status: Additional silhouette concept; no replacement, provenance, material certification or production approval claimed
